description: Factors, multiples, and the HCF/LCM toolkit

lessons.title: Factors and Multiples
lessons.intro: Factors divide a number exactly; multiples are what you get by skip-counting. They are two sides of the same coin!
explanation: A factor of 12 divides 12 with no remainder: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12.
A multiple of 5 is 5, 10, 15, 20, ... — the times table of 5.
Factors are smaller-or-equal; multiples grow bigger.
lessons.rule: Factors divide exactly; multiples are skip-counts.
lessons.tip: Factors come in pairs that multiply to the number.

steps.text: A factor divides with no remainder.
A multiple is the number times a whole number.

lessons.title: Finding All Factors
lessons.intro: To list every factor, test numbers in pairs from 1 upwards.
explanation: Each pair gives two factors at once.
Stop when the pair numbers meet in the middle.
lessons.rule: Find factor pairs from 1 up to the square root.
lessons.tip: Every number has 1 and itself as factors.

lessons.title: Multiples Grow Forever
lessons.intro: A number has endless multiples — you can always find the next one.
explanation: Multiples of 8: 8, 16, 24, 32, ...
The 4th multiple of 5 is 20.
Multiples never stop; factors always do.
lessons.rule: Multiples are endless; find any by multiplying.
lessons.tip: The nth multiple = number x n.

lessons.title: Common Factors
lessons.intro: Two numbers can share factors — these are called common factors.
explanation: Common factors: 1, 2, 3, 6.
The biggest shared one is special (that is the HCF!).
lessons.rule: Common factors appear in both factor lists.
lessons.tip: 1 is always a common factor.

lessons.title: Common Multiples
lessons.intro: Two numbers also share multiples — the common multiples.
explanation: Multiples of 4: 4,8,12,16,... Multiples of 6: 6,12,18,...
Common multiples: 12, 24, 36, ...
The smallest shared one is special (that is the LCM!).
lessons.rule: Common multiples appear in both multiple lists.
lessons.tip: The smallest common multiple is the LCM.

quiz.question: How many factors does 6 have?
What is the largest factor of 20 other than 20 itself?
What is the 4th multiple of 5?
Is 7 a factor of 56? Answer Yes or No.
Meena has 12 chocolates to arrange in equal rows. How many different numbers of equal rows are possible (count all factors of 12)?
What is the smallest multiple of 8 that is greater than 20?
What is the greatest common factor of 12 and 18?
What is the smallest number that is a multiple of both 4 and 6?
quiz.hint: List multiples of each and find the first match.

lessons.title: What is HCF?
lessons.intro: The Highest Common Factor is the biggest number that divides two numbers exactly.
explanation: HCF of 12 and 18: common factors are 1,2,3,6; the highest is 6.
HCF is always less than or equal to the smaller number.
It is also called the Greatest Common Divisor (GCD).
lessons.rule: HCF = the largest factor shared by both numbers.
lessons.tip: List factors of both, pick the biggest shared one.

steps.text: List the factors of each number.
The biggest shared factor is the HCF.

lessons.title: HCF by Listing
lessons.intro: The simplest way to find HCF is to list factors and spot the biggest match.
explanation: HCF of 8 and 12: factors 1,2,4,8 and 1,2,3,4,6,12.
Shared: 1,2,4. Highest is 4.
Listing is reliable for small numbers.
lessons.rule: Match the factor lists and take the largest.
lessons.tip: Underline the shared factors.

lessons.title: When HCF is 1
lessons.intro: Some number pairs share only the factor 1 — we call them co-prime.
explanation: HCF of 9 and 16 is 1.
They have no common factor except 1.
Co-prime numbers need not be prime themselves.
lessons.rule: If the only common factor is 1, numbers are co-prime.
lessons.tip: Co-prime does not mean prime.

lessons.title: HCF in Real Life
lessons.intro: HCF helps when we want the largest equal groups or pieces.
explanation: Cutting 24 cm and 36 cm ribbons into the longest equal pieces uses HCF.
HCF of 24 and 36 is 12, so each piece is 12 cm.
The 'largest equal' clue means HCF.
lessons.rule: 'Largest equal size/group' problems use HCF.
lessons.tip: Look for the word 'largest' or 'greatest'.

lessons.title: HCF of Three Numbers
lessons.intro: You can find the HCF of three numbers by taking the common factor of all three.
explanation: HCF of 16, 24, 40: all are divisible by 8.
Check the largest number that divides every one.
8 is the HCF.
lessons.rule: HCF of three = largest factor common to all three.
lessons.tip: Find HCF of two first, then with the third.

quiz.question: What is the HCF of 12 and 18?
What is the HCF of 8 and 12?
What is the HCF of 15 and 25?
What is the HCF of 9 and 16?
Two ribbons are 24 cm and 36 cm. They are cut into equal pieces of the greatest possible length. How long is each piece, in cm?
Trays hold 30 and 45 sweets. What is the greatest number of sweets per equal group that empties both?
What is the HCF of 48 and 60?
What is the HCF of 16, 24 and 40?

lessons.title: What is LCM?
lessons.intro: The Lowest Common Multiple is the smallest number that two numbers both divide into.
explanation: LCM of 4 and 6: common multiples 12, 24, ...; the lowest is 12.
LCM is always greater than or equal to the larger number.
It is the first time both times-tables meet.
lessons.rule: LCM = the smallest multiple shared by both numbers.
lessons.tip: List multiples of the larger number and test each.

steps.text: The first shared multiple is the LCM.

lessons.title: LCM by Listing
lessons.intro: List the multiples of the bigger number and check which one the smaller also divides.
explanation: LCM of 3 and 5: 5,10,15 — 15 is divisible by 3.
Checking the bigger number's multiples is faster.
Stop at the first common one.
lessons.rule: Test multiples of the larger number first.
lessons.tip: This saves time versus listing both.

lessons.title: LCM of Co-prime Numbers
lessons.intro: If two numbers share no factors, their LCM is simply their product.
explanation: LCM of 3 and 5 is 15 = 3 x 5.
This shortcut works only for co-prime numbers.
Otherwise the LCM is smaller than the product.
lessons.rule: Co-prime numbers: LCM = their product.
lessons.tip: Check they share no factor before multiplying.

lessons.title: LCM in Real Life
lessons.intro: LCM helps when events repeat together — like bells or blinking lights.
explanation: Bells every 4 and 6 minutes ring together after the LCM: 12 minutes.
The 'next time together' clue means LCM.
Lights blinking every 8 and 12 seconds sync after 24 seconds.
lessons.rule: 'Next time together / least' problems use LCM.
lessons.tip: Look for 'together again' or 'smallest'.

lessons.title: LCM of Three Numbers
lessons.intro: Find the LCM of three numbers step by step: two first, then with the third.
explanation: Work in pairs to keep it simple.
24 is divisible by 4, 6 and 8.
lessons.rule: LCM of three = build it two numbers at a time.
lessons.tip: Do the first pair, then combine with the third.

quiz.question: What is the LCM of 4 and 6?
What is the LCM of 3 and 5?
What is the LCM of 6 and 8?
What is the LCM of 10 and 15?
Two bells ring every 4 and 6 minutes. After how many minutes do they ring together again?
Two lights blink every 8 and 12 seconds. After how many seconds do they blink together?
What is the LCM of 12 and 18?
What is the LCM of 4, 6 and 8?

lessons.title: Prime Factorisation
lessons.intro: Every number can be broken into a product of prime numbers — its prime factorisation.
explanation: Primes are numbers with exactly two factors: 1 and themselves.
Keep dividing by the smallest prime until you reach 1.
lessons.rule: Prime factorisation writes a number as primes multiplied.
lessons.tip: Start dividing by 2, then 3, then 5...

steps.text: Divide by the smallest prime repeatedly.
The prime factors multiply back to the number.

lessons.title: Building Numbers from Primes
lessons.intro: Multiply prime factors together to rebuild the original number.
explanation: The order of primes does not matter.
lessons.rule: Multiply the primes back to get the number.
lessons.tip: Group repeated primes to multiply faster.

lessons.title: HCF from Prime Factors
lessons.intro: Take the primes COMMON to both numbers to build the HCF.
explanation: Common primes: 2x2x3 = 12.
HCF uses the shared primes only.
lessons.rule: HCF = product of common prime factors.
lessons.tip: Pick primes that appear in both.

lessons.title: LCM from Prime Factors
lessons.intro: Take ALL primes, using the highest count from either number, to build the LCM.
explanation: LCM = 2x2x3x3 = 36.
Include every prime at its biggest power.
lessons.rule: LCM = product of all primes at highest powers.
lessons.tip: Never miss a prime that appears in either number.

lessons.title: Prime Factor Puzzles
lessons.intro: Knowing a number's primes lets you solve many puzzles quickly.
explanation: A number with primes 2, 3, 5 each once is 30.
A number = 2 x 2 x 7 is 28.
Prime factors are a number's 'fingerprint'.
lessons.rule: A number's prime factors uniquely identify it.
lessons.tip: Multiply the given primes to find the number.

quiz.question: What is the smallest prime number?
What is 2 x 2 x 3?
In the prime factorisation 18 = 2 x 3 x 3, what is the largest prime factor?
What is 2 x 2 x 2 x 3?
A number's prime factors are 2, 3 and 5, each used once. What is the number?
A number equals 2 x 2 x 7. What is the number?
quiz.story: Rebuilding a number from its primes.

quiz.question: Using prime factors, what is the HCF of 36 and 48?
Using prime factors, what is the LCM of 9 and 12?

lessons.title: Choosing HCF or LCM
lessons.intro: The trick in word problems is deciding whether to use HCF or LCM.
explanation: 'Largest/greatest equal' -> HCF.
'Smallest/least, together again' -> LCM.
Read the question's clue words carefully.
lessons.rule: HCF for largest-equal; LCM for least-together.
lessons.tip: Spot the clue word first, then calculate.

lessons.title: Sharing Equally (HCF)
lessons.intro: When splitting into the biggest equal groups, HCF gives the group size.
explanation: 36 and 60 sweets into equal largest groups: HCF(36,60)=12.
Each group has 12 of each kind.
Largest-equal always points to HCF.
lessons.rule: Largest equal share = HCF of the amounts.
lessons.tip: The answer is never bigger than the smaller amount.

lessons.title: Meeting Again (LCM)
lessons.intro: When repeating events line up, LCM gives the meeting time.
explanation: Buses every 15 and 20 minutes meet after LCM = 60 min.
The next-together time is the LCM.
Both schedules fit the LCM exactly.
lessons.rule: Next-together time = LCM of the intervals.
lessons.tip: The answer is never smaller than the larger interval.

lessons.title: Mixed Clues
lessons.intro: Some problems hide the clue — rephrase them in your own words.
explanation: 'Cut into equal longest pieces' -> HCF.
'Ring together / smallest number divisible' -> LCM.
Turning the words into 'largest' or 'smallest' helps.
lessons.rule: Reword the problem to reveal HCF or LCM.
lessons.tip: Ask: am I splitting or syncing?

lessons.title: HCF & LCM Master
lessons.intro: Put both skills together and pick the right tool every time.
explanation: Smallest number divisible by 6, 8, 12 -> LCM = 24.
Largest number dividing 60 and 90 -> HCF = 30.
Confidence comes from reading the clue words.
lessons.rule: Match the clue to the right tool, then compute.
lessons.tip: Double-check with a quick division.

quiz.question: What is the HCF of 20 and 30?
What is the LCM of 5 and 7?

What is the largest number that divides both 60 and 90 exactly?
